The Ten Essentials Be prepared before you go outdoors! Pack these categories depending on the intensity of your hike. NAVIGATION SUNSCREEN WATER KNIFE SHELTER Map and compass, GPS unit, or a local trail map. Know your destination and the surrouding area. Lotion, sunglasses, or even a wide-brimmed hat. Protect yourself from sunburns, including in winter. Bring more than needed, or a purification method. Leave extra in your car for the end of the trip. For gear repairs, food preparation, making kindling, and more. A multitool can offer more flexibility. Just in case you spend the night unexpectedly. Think emergency blanket, not a tent back at camp! CLOTHING LIGHT FOOD FIRE FIRST AID A base to keep warm, and a shell to keep dry. Dress in layers that you can swap during the day. Don’t forget to charge it or pack extra batteries! A headlamp is a great hands-free option. Choose something that will sustain your energy. Items with a long shelf life can last multiple trips. Waterproof matches, a lighter, and/or a tinderbox. Consider a portable stove in areas without firewood. Get familiar with your kit before an emergency. Include ointments and bandages for blisters.
